t.4.36.1: Thus addressed by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva spoke these words to Hanumān, his minister, who stood at his side.
t.4.36.2: Those who dwell on the peaks of Mahendra, Himavat, Vindhya and Kailāsa, on Mandara, on the white-peaked mountain, and on the Pañcaśaila mountains,
t.4.36.4: And on the mountain that is the abode of Āditya, resembling the clouds at twilight, the foremost of the monkeys have taken shelter in the fearsome forest of lotuses and palmyra palms.
t.4.36.3: And those who dwell in the western quarter, on the mountains at the ocean's edge that have the hue of the newly risen sun and shine resplendent on every side...
t.4.36.5: Those monkeys who dwell on Mount Añjana, resembling collyrium-dark clouds and possessing the might of elephants.
t.4.36.6: The golden-hued vānaras who dwell in the caves of red arsenic, those who live on the slopes of Meru, and those who have taken refuge on Dhūmragiri.
t.4.36.7: And those monkeys of fearsome speed, having the hue of the rising sun, who dwell on the mountain Mahāruṇa drinking honey-wine.
t.4.36.8: In very lovely forests, fragrant and vast, and all around in the delightful forest borders of the ascetics.
t.4.36.9: Swiftly bring all those monkeys, each and every one, who dwell upon the earth; and by means such as conciliation and gifts, quickly dispatch the monkeys.
t.4.36.11: Those monkeys who are attached to pleasures and those who are dilatory, bring them all here quickly by my command.
t.4.36.10: There are the very swift messengers who were sent out by me at first; now, to hasten them, you must send forth yet other monkeys once more.
t.4.36.12: And those who do not come within ten days at my command, those evil-minded ones who defile the king's decree, are to be slain.
t.4.36.14: Let the foremost of monkeys, terrible in form, resembling clouds and mountains, go forth from here at my command, as though covering the sky.
t.4.36.13: By my command, let hundreds, thousands and crores of lion-like monkeys, abiding by my will, set out toward the quarters of the world.
t.4.36.15: Let all those monkeys who know the ways, having gone their way across the earth, swiftly bring all the monkeys here at my command.
t.4.36.16: Having heard the words of that king of the monkeys, the son of Vāyu dispatched valiant monkeys in all directions.
t.4.36.18: Those monkeys urged on all the monkeys in the oceans, on the mountains, in the forests and along the rivers, for the sake of Rāma.
t.4.36.17: Sent forth by the king, those monkeys, travelling the path of birds and stars, set out at that very instant into the region over which Viṣṇu once strode.
t.4.36.19: Having heard the command of Sugrīva, the king of kings, who was like Death and Time, the monkeys came, seeing cause for fear in Sugrīva.
t.4.36.20: Then from that mountain three crores of monkeys, resembling collyrium and of great speed, set forth to where Rāghava was.
t.4.36.22: And then from the peaks of Kailāsa came thousands of crores of vānaras, whose radiance was like the mane of a lion.
t.4.36.21: From that best of mountains where the sun goes to its setting, ten koṭis of monkeys who delight in dwelling there, gleaming like molten gold, have set forth.
t.4.36.23: Living on fruits and roots and dwelling on Himavant, of them a thousand times a thousand crores came together.
t.4.36.25: Those who dwell on the shores of the Ocean of Milk, those who live in the tamāla forests, and those who feed on coconuts, of them there is no counting.
t.4.36.24: From the Vindhya there swiftly came down thousands of crores of monkeys, fearsome and of fearsome deeds, glowing like Aṅgāraka.
t.4.36.26: From the forests, from the thickets and from the rivers came the swift monkey army, as though drinking up the sun.
t.4.36.27: But those vānaras who had gone to hasten all the vānaras, those heroes, beheld the mountain Himavat, covered with mighty trees.
t.4.36.28: On that delightful, excellent mountain, long ago, a sacrifice dedicated to Maheśvara shone forth, divine and captivating, gladdening the hearts of all the gods.
t.4.36.30: Whoever eats even once that heavenly, delightful fruit and root, which has grown as food, remains satisfied for a month.
t.4.36.29: There the vānaras saw roots and fruits, sprung from an overflowing abundance of food, nearly as sweet to the taste as nectar.
t.4.36.32: And going to that place of sacrifice, the vānaras brought back fragrant flowers as well, for the sake of doing what was pleasing to Sugrīva.
t.4.36.31: The fruit-eating leaders of the monkey troops took those divine roots and fruits, and divine medicinal herbs as well.
t.4.36.33: And all those foremost monkeys, having quickly urged on all the monkeys upon the earth, went at the head of their troops.
t.4.36.34: And those troop-leaders, swift in action, reached Kiṣkindhā in haste within that very moment, to where the monkey Sugrīva was.
t.4.36.35: Those monkeys, having gathered all the medicinal herbs, fruits and roots, made him accept them, and spoke these words.
t.4.36.36: All the mountains, the oceans and the forests have been ranged over, and all the monkeys on the earth are coming at your command.
t.4.36.37: Having heard this, Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, was delighted, and, pleased, he accepted all the gifts they had brought.
